title: A uniform Frobenius power gives a sheaf norm for the reduction immersion
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that it has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $p\mathcal O_X=0$ (in every local ring). Write $i:X_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$ for the reduction immersion and $\mathcal N_X$ for its nilradical [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. There exist an integer $e\geq1$ and unital ring homomorphisms $$
u_V:\Gamma(i^{-1}V,\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{red}}})\longrightarrow\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$$ for every open $V\subseteq X$, compatible with restriction, such that $
u_V(i^\sharp a)=a^{p^e}$ for every $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$. On each affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, under $\Gamma(i^{-1}U,\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{red}}})=A/\sqrt{(0)}$, the map is $ ar a\mapsto a^{p^e}$. Moreover, for every open $V$, every $b\in\Gamma(i^{-1}V,\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{red}}})$ and every $y\in i^{-1}V$, $$b(y)=0\ \Longrightarrow\ 
u_V(b)(i(y))=0,$$ where values are taken in residue fields [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], $i$ is the identity on underlying spaces and $i_*\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{red}}}=\mathcal O_X/\mathcal N_X$ as sheaves of rings. Apply [lem-sc-reduction-nilradical-nilpotent] to the Noetherian scheme $X$ and choose $n\geq1$ such that $\mathcal N_X^n=0$. This is one exponent on all of $X$, not an exponent chosen separately for each open. Choose $e\geq1$ with $q=p^e\geq n$, possible because $p\geq2$. Then $\mathcal N_X^q=0$: a product of $q$ local sections of $\mathcal N_X$ contains a product of $n$ such sections, which is zero.

proof.text: For every open $W\subseteq X$, the element $p\cdot1\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$ is zero: its germ is zero at every point by hypothesis, hence it is zero by the sheaf separatedness axiom. By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $P_W:a\mapsto a^q$ is a unital ring endomorphism, and it commutes with restriction since restriction is a ring homomorphism and preserves powers. The zero section ring, in particular the ring on the empty open, is allowed: there the power map is the unique ring endomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0CC6 (varieties-section-frobenius), paragraph after Definition 03SM (varieties-definition-absolute-frobenius), iterated e times; applied in the construction of 0BDZ.

proof.text: Fix an open $V$ and $b\in\Gamma(i^{-1}V,\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{red}}})$. The quotient-sheaf description in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] means that $b$ has lifts $a_j\in\Gamma(W_j,\mathcal O_X)$ on an open cover $V=\bigcup_jW_j$: a quotient germ has a representative, and equality of germs holds on a smaller neighbourhood. If $a$ and $a^\prime$ are two lifts on an open $W$, then $a-a^\prime\in\mathcal N_X(W)$. Its $q$-th power is zero by Step 1 (equivalently, its germ belongs to the $q$-th power of the nilradical at each point). By the ring-endomorphism assertion of [def-weil-ring-frobenius], $a^q-(a^\prime)^q=(a-a^\prime)^q=0$. Applying this to restricted lifts on each $W_j\cap W_k$ shows that their $q$-th powers agree. No affineness of these intersections is used.

source.place: Tag 0BDZ (divisors-lemma-Frobenius-gives-norm-for-reduction), proof; the local-lift gluing details omitted there.

proof.text:
The sheaf axiom for the structure sheaf of the scheme [def-pc-scheme] now gives a unique section $
u_V(b)$ restricting to $a_j^q$ on each $W_j$. Step 3 applied to any two systems of lifts shows independence of both lifts and cover. For two sections $b,c$, pass to the intersections of their lifting covers. On such an open, if $a,d$ lift $b,c$, then $a+d$, $ad$, and $1$ lift $b+c$, $bc$, and $1$. By [def-weil-ring-frobenius], their $q$-th powers are $a^q+d^q$, $a^qd^q$, and $1$. Equality locally implies equality globally, so $
u_V$ is a unital ring homomorphism. If $V^\prime\subseteq V$, restrict the same lifts to $W_j\cap V^\prime$; restriction preserves powers, and uniqueness of gluing gives $
u_V(b)|_{V^\prime}=
u_{V^\prime}(b|_{i^{-1}V^\prime})$.

proof.text: For $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$, the section $a$ itself is a lift of $i^\sharp a$, so the construction gives $\nu_V(i^\sharp a)=a^q$. For any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the affine description of the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies $i^\sharp$ with a surjection $A\to A/J$. Its kernel is $\mathcal N_X(U)=\sqrt{(0)}$ by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]; hence $J=\sqrt{(0)}$ and $\Gamma(i^{-1}U,\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{red}}})=A/\sqrt{(0)}$. Every class $\bar a$ has the global lift $a$, so the displayed affine formula is exactly $\bar a\mapsto a^q$. This verifies the formula on every affine open, not just on a chosen cover.

source.place: Tag 0BDZ (divisors-lemma-Frobenius-gives-norm-for-reduction), proof; the local-lift gluing details omitted there.

proof.text: Let $y\in i^{-1}V$, put $x=i(y)$, and choose one local lift $a$ of $b$ near $x$. By the residue-field map of [def-weil-residue-field], the image of $a(x)\in\kappa(x)$ in $\kappa(y)$ is $b(y)$. A unital homomorphism of fields is injective (if a nonzero element maps to zero, multiplying by its inverse would give $1=0$). Thus $b(y)=0$ implies $a(x)=0$. The constructed section equals $a^q$ near $x$, so $\nu_V(b)(x)=a(x)^q=0$. If $V$ is empty the construction is the unique homomorphism between zero rings and this clause is vacuous.

lean.statement: theorem reduction_frobenius_sheaf_norm (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hchar : ∀ x : X, (p : X.presheaf.stalk x) = 0) : ∃ e : ℕ, 1 ≤ e ∧ ∃ ν : ∀ V : X.Opens, Γ(X.nilradical.subscheme, X.nilradical.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ V) →+* Γ(X, V), (∀ (V W : X.Opens) (hVW : V ≤ W) (b : Γ(X.nilradical.subscheme, X.nilradical.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ W)), X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hVW).op (ν W b) = ν V (X.nilradical.subscheme.presheaf.map (homOfLE (X.nilradical.subschemeι.preimage_mono hVW)).op b)) ∧ (∀ (V : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, V)), ν V (X.nilradical.subschemeι.app V a) = a ^ (p ^ e)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (a : Γ(X, U.1)), ν U.1 ((X.nilradical.subschemeObjIso U).inv (Ideal.Quotient.mk (X.nilradical.ideal U) a)) = a ^ (p ^ e)) ∧ (∀ (V : X.Opens) (b : Γ(X.nilradical.subscheme, X.nilradical.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ V)) (y : X.nilradical.subscheme) (hy : y ∈ X.nilradical.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ V), X.nilradical.subscheme.evaluation (X.nilradical.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ V) y hy b = 0 → X.evaluation V (X.nilradical.subschemeι y) hy (ν V b) = 0)
